caseStudy.name: Tsho Rolpa glacial lake, Rolwaling, Nepal

bookmarks.name: Tsho Rolpa lake
bookmarks.basis: Around the lake edge measured from the radar, padded 0.01°.

bookmarks.name: Rolwaling valley
bookmarks.basis: The whole radar clip, about 12 by 9 km.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Radar backdrop (median HV)

explanation.what: The median HV radar brightness of all dates, used as a quiet background.
explanation.inspect: Use it to find your way around the valley.

limitations: A median of several dates, so it belongs to no single date.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Radar brightness (HH)
layers.unitsNote: Gamma-0 backscatter, linear in the file, shown in dB.

legend.highLabel: Bright: rough rock, slopes facing the radar

explanation.what: How much of the radar pulse bounced back to NISAR on each date. HH means sent and received horizontally.
explanation.measures: Backscatter strength. Calm water acts like a mirror and sends the pulse away, so the lake is dark.
explanation.inspect: Step through the dates and watch the dark lake shape. Click a point to read the stored value.
explanation.establishes: Where open water and rough surfaces are on each date. It does not show depth or water level.

limitations: Provisional data: calibrated and partly validated, not for final scientific conclusions.
Dates alternate between dual-pol 10 m and quad-pol 20 m acquisitions. All are shown on a shared 20 m grid.
Radar shadow behind steep slopes also looks dark. Shadows do not change between dates on this track, so they do not move.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Colour radar (HH, HV, HH/HV)

keys.label: Black: calm water, or radar shadow
Purple: smooth bare rock, ice, snow
Bright blobs: steep slopes facing the radar (distorted)

explanation.what: Two radar channels and their ratio mixed into one colour picture.
explanation.measures: Red is HH brightness, green is HV (which rises with rough, jumbled surfaces such as debris and vegetation), blue is HH divided by HV.
explanation.inspect: The lake is near black. Smooth rock, ice and snow look purple. Rough moraines and debris look yellow-green. Bright blobs are steep slopes squashed by the radar's side view.
explanation.establishes: A visual guide only. Colours are not measurements, so the inspector does not sample this layer.

limitations: Provisional data: calibrated and partly validated, not for final scientific conclusions.
Dates alternate between dual-pol 10 m and quad-pol 20 m acquisitions. All are shown on a shared 20 m grid.
Radar shadow behind steep slopes also looks dark. Shadows do not change between dates on this track, so they do not move.
Colours are stretched for display. Compare shapes between dates, not exact colours.

layers.name: Lake edge measured from radar
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NISAR GCOV (NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, ASF DAAC)
limitations: Drawn from radar at 20 m: edges are accurate to about one or two pixels (20 to 40 m).
All dates are drawn on top of each other. Where they overlap, the lake edge did not move.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Ground stability (16–28 Aug)

explanation.what: How alike the radar echoes were on 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-28, from 0 (nothing alike) to 1 (identical).
explanation.measures: Interferometric coherence. Bare rock and the moraine dam stay bright. Water, moving ice and fresh snow go dark.
explanation.inspect: Look at the dam at the lake's western end: if it were slumping or soaking it would turn dark.
explanation.establishes: Where the surface stayed the same for 12 days. It does not say how far anything moved.

limitations: Steep slopes facing away from the radar are dark because of radar shadow, not change.
Twelve days in the monsoon: wet snow and rain lower coherence even on stable ground.

layers.name: Dam and glacier zones tested for movement
limitations: The dam zone is a 500 m circle at the lake's lowest shore. The glacier zone is a 2.5 km circle beyond the far end of the lake. No glacier outline is loaded, so this zone is approximate.

layers.attribution: Scenario by CascadeLens from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and the NISAR lake area
layers.name: River route below the dam
limitations: Traced on a 60 m terrain model with depressions filled. It follows the valley floor, not the exact river channel.

layers.attribution: Scenario by CascadeLens from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and the NISAR lake area
layers.name: Flooded area if a 20 m breach (scenario)
limitations: Scenario only: the widest case (highest peak flow, smoothest channel) for a 20 m breach, from 60 m terrain cross-sections every 500 m.
The peak is not reduced downstream, so the area is larger than a real flood of this size would cover far from the lake.

layers.name: Terrain shading (Copernicus DEM)

explanation.what: Shaded relief of the valleys below the lake.
explanation.measures: Nothing: light and shadow from the terrain heights.
explanation.inspect: Use it to follow the river route.

limitations: Shading only, from 60 m averaged heights.

lake.name: Tsho Rolpa
lake.basin: Rolwaling Khola, then Tamakoshi and Sun Koshi, in the Koshi Basin
lake.published: Published surveys give about 1.5 to 1.6 km² for Tsho Rolpa in the 2010s and 2020s.

terrain.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30: © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
terrain.note: Heights from Copernicus DEM (2011 to 2015 survey), not from NISAR. The radar is draped on top.

lake.method: Dark area in HH + HV below -7 dB after 3x3 smoothing on a 20 m grid. The range reruns it at -6 and -8 dB.

motion.zonesNote: The dam zone is a 500 m circle at the lake's lowest shore. The glacier zone is a 2.5 km circle beyond the far end of the lake. No glacier outline is loaded, so this zone is approximate.
